title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Solicitor's Lien - Prejudice to Client
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client fires their paralegal the day before a major Small Claims Court trial and demands their original file documents. The client owes the paralegal $1,000 in unpaid fees. Can the paralegal assert a solicitor's lien and withhold the file until payment is made?
options: Yes, a solicitor's lien is absolute and always applies to unpaid accounts.
No, a paralegal cannot assert a retaining lien if withholding the documents would materially prejudice the client's position in an ongoing proceeding.
Yes, provided the paralegal gets an order from the trial judge first.
No, solicitor's liens only apply to trust account funds, not physical files.
questions.explain: While a legal practitioner has a common-law right to a retaining lien (solicitor's lien) over client property for unpaid fees, the Rules of Conduct specify that a practitioner must not enforce this lien if doing so would materially prejudice the client. Withholding the entire file the day before trial clearly causes material prejudice.
